examples.name: Collapsible
examples.code:
() => {
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
return (
  <Box align="start">
    <Button primary onClick={() => setOpen(!open)} label="Toggle" />
    <Collapsible open={open}>
      <Box
        background="light-2"
        round="medium"
        pad="medium"
        align="center"
        justify="center"
      >
        <Text>This is a box inside a Collapsible component</Text>
      </Box>
    </Collapsible>
    <Text>This is other content outside the Collapsible box</Text>
  </Box>
)}

prose.title: React/DOM Properties
prose.text:
At its core, the Collapsible component is a regular <div> element. Thus, both DOM and React properties, methods, and events are accessible. To read up on all of the possible DOM attributes and types available for div elements, check out this [MDN Web Documents page.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/div) To learn more about DOM events and methods, you can read more on the [MDN Web Events documentation page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Events).

Also, feel free to read about the [types of React events available](https://reactjs.org/docs/handling-events.html), or see [how DOM attributes change in React.](https://reactjs.org/docs/dom-elements.html) Working in tandem with Styled Components, you also have access to the [as property.](https://styled-components.com/docs/api#as-polymorphic-prop)
